title: The Impact of the Gig Economy on Product Quality Through the Labor Market: Evidence from Ridesharing and Restaurant Quality
authors: Minkyu Shin; Jiwoong Shin; Soheil Ghili; Jaehwan Kim
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Single treated city (Austin) vs. control (Dallas restaurants in the shipped Yelp data); Uber/Lyft present before 2016-05, absent 2016-05 to 2017-04, present again from 2017-05. Common dates for all treated units.
eligible_reason: Not staggered. One treated city (Austin) with rideshare exit (May 2016) and re-entry (May 2017) at common dates; felm(y ~ austin:(month<2016-05) + austin:(month>=2017-05) | rest_id + month | 0 | rest_id) with two treatment regressors (pre-exit and post-reentry periods) relative to the exit period. No variation in adoption timing across treated units. The turnover analysis (Tables 7-9) is a Cox proportional hazards model on synthetic data.
design_notes: R lfe::felm with restaurant and month FE, clustered by restaurant. Yelp review sentiment outcomes: neg_label_rate_service (Table 3, and by price tier Tables 5-6), neg_label_rate_food (Table 4). Shipped Yelp panel main_did_dat_all_dal.Rdata: 58,227 restaurant-months (Austin 17,699; Dallas 40,528), 2014-05 to 2019-05. Turnover: coxph with restaurant and month dummies, position FE, hourly wage, Austin x before/after indicators.

specs.exclusion_reason: single treated city with common exit/re-entry dates (not staggered); two treatment regressors (austin x pre-exit, austin x post-reentry)
Cox proportional hazards (nonlinear), time-varying wage control, single treated DMA, synthetic data

data_files_note: Yelp review-sentiment panel shipped (scraped, processed); employee turnover data are under NDA and replaced by synthetic data.
data_provenance_note: Yelp panel is the processed analysis data (original); turnover data are synthetic (README).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Not a staggered design: single treated city with common on/off dates.
